proposed_description: The present for saying the weather: impersonal fare + weather word (fa caldo, fa freddo, fa bel tempo, che tempo fa?), the subjectless weather verbs (piove, nevica, tira vento), and the contrast that polices the boundary: essere for a THING's temperature (il caffè è caldo) against fare for the ambient day. The defining trap is the English calque: 'it is hot' copied as è caldo, which misdescribes weather as an object. English props these sentences up with 'it'; Italian uses no subject at all.

proposed_attributes.canonical_example: Fa caldo; D'inverno fa freddo; Piove; Che tempo fa?
proposed_attributes.common_miss: è caldo / è freddo for ambient weather (the English to-be calque)

rationale: Commissioned by Smith 2026-08-03 (option (a) on the OPEN_QUESTIONS 2026-07-21 entry raised from his live translation mark): impersonal weather fare had no present-tense home, and verb_form.imperfect.usage.age_time_weather is the precedent for giving it one. Label reasoning (criterion 15): 'Weather expressions' names the DOMAIN, not the verb - a label naming fare would hand over exactly the verb choice the items test, and the deliberate contrast item (pu_wthr_03, essere for a thing's temperature) relies on the visible breadcrumb TEMPTING fa, which its must_not catches. Boundary: c'è-weather (c'è il sole, c'è vento) is deliberately excluded - esserci is ExistentialAuthor's carve-out; this leaf holds fare-weather and the subjectless weather verbs.
